invalid_instantaneous_peak.evidence_strength: The source mechanism and slow-PSS/fast-next-sample sequence explain the anomalous number; this is a measurement interpretation, not a rerun or reconstructed exact instantaneous utilization.
invalid_instantaneous_peak.report_instead: Permutation phase: 1081.514855149 CPU seconds /22.7482480276376 wall seconds =47.542775770469525 average core-equivalents; maximum sampled live/running worker counts 61/61.
invalid_instantaneous_peak.source_explanation: telemetry._process reads each process CPU then its potentially slow smaps_rollup. Monitor.sample timestamps only after all sequential process/PSS scans. The slow previous sample therefore aggregates CPU at unequal, earlier effective times than its end timestamp; the next short non-PSS sample can divide a longer effective CPU interval by about two wall seconds. Bracketing RUSAGE_CHILDREN detects reaping races but not this skew. The saved trace does not contain individual CPU-read timestamps, so an exact corrected instantaneous peak cannot be recovered.

caveats: Sampled live/running counts are successive per-process observations, not a simultaneous timestamp for every state.
Worker ru_maxrss includes inherited/shared pages and prior work in that worker; summing it is not physical memory consumption.
PSS sums are sequentially sampled approximations; 62-process coverage at the largest observed sum is parent plus 61 children.
Host available memory includes unrelated host state and is not a proof of the unique limiting resource.

scope: Saved metadata arithmetic and source-level explanation only. No scientific modules imported, labels regenerated, predictions recomputed, or experiments rerun. Frozen raw trace and results remain unchanged.
